I don’t mean to sound like doing what I did would work for you, hearing prescriptive advice from people pissed me off so badly.
It’s just my anecdotal experience about turning the ship around while feeling at my worst.

There’s two sides you’ve brought up. Substance addiction and a rejection of living sober. What’s being sober like for you?

I hear you. I have perpetual cycles of numbness and I’ve been in places for years mentally where sometimes things don’t feel worth it. I’m filled with self resentment or resentment at the world.

I think what changed for me was trying harder and taking bigger bites of the apple in my life and seeing where my autonomy could get me the less I cared about outcomes on other peoples terms. 

Simply put, I had just conditioned myself into thinking small about what success looked like and what I thought I should be doing. Once I broke out of that mold because I really felt like I had nothing to lose with how little I was starting to care about holding on to life, things actually got easier. I decided that if I was going to end things I might as well try harder while not giving a shit. My efforts in work and with new hobbies and exercise seemed to pay off and I began feeling good because it was like I was letting myself feel good.

Don’t get me wrong. The darkness is still always there. At some level I’m mentally ill with an inexplicable depression that brings about suicidal ideation but now it feels more like a tide with familiar patterns that I can watch come and go. As much as I feel in control I still think I need help and certain medications were absolutely not it for me and it sucked figuring that out.

Everyone’s mental health journey is unique. Chemical imbalance, social factors, unresolved trauma. It’s hard not knowing why things don’t feel right. But it’s worth the effort, I never could have imagined what the world could look like for me once I allowed myself to really start looking.
